newsitem.title: ITALY: Investigators raise heat on Italy's League.
newsitem.headline: Investigators raise heat on Italy's League.

text.p: Police searched offices of the separatist Northern League party and members' homes on Wednesday on the orders of a prosecutor investigating alleged criminal attempts to undermine the unity of Italy.

The searches, branded a "fascist" crackdown by the party, took place as President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro urged parliament to respond to the northern discontent at the root of the League's appeal with urgent reforms to the way Italy is governed.
The chief prosecutor in the northern town of Verona, Guido Papalia, said he had ordered the searches on suspicion that League officials were engaged in anti-constitutional activities.
The League said the investigations were directed against three organisers of the party's "green shirts", an unarmed security squad formed earlier this year by leader Umberto Bossi.

Senior League politician Roberto Maroni said police had also attempted to enter and search the League's Milan headquarters but had left after he informed them that one of the three men, Corinto Marchini, did not have an office there.
Marchini and the other suspects, Verona officials Enzo Flego and Sandrino Speri, had their offices or homes searched in Wednesday's inquiries.

The searches coincided with mounting calls for criminal action against the League and its leader Bossi following a "declaration of independence" in Venice on Sunday for the movement's self-styled northern "republic of Padania".

Scalfaro, in a rare message to both houses of parliament, said the state had the instruments at its disposal to respond to any breach of the law but told the legislature that the response to Bossi's breakaway bid must be primarily political.
He urged parliamentarians to display "the broadest political will" as they begin to debate constitutional reforms that are expected to include a new federal structure for Italy.

"There are reasons for protest. It's up to you to identify them, study them and confront them with courage and determination without losing time on diatribe and differences. I don't think there is room for that any more," he said.

Bossi's League has thrived on popular frustration in affluent northern Italy with stifling central government bureaucracy, high taxes and public sector inefficiency, winning 10.6 percent of votes at a general election last April.
Bossi failed to attract anywhere near the one million plus followers he had hoped to draw to a separatist trek along the River Po last weekend, which climaxed in the Venice declaration.
But Scalfaro said discontent in the north had to be tackled.
"Let us not make the mistake of thinking that now that the demonstrations are over, the question is closed," he said. "... don't ignore the malaise at the root of so much discontent".
Bossi dismissed Scalfaro's message as empty words.
"They say one thing in parliament then the facts show they adopt fascist-style methods," he said of Wednesday's searches.
Bossi and other League officials face several separate investigations by magistrates in a number of northern towns.

Among alleged offences being investigated are "attacking the integrity and unity of the state", which can carry a life prison sentence on conviction, attacking the constitution and violating bans on forming military associations and secret societies.
